R123 revision 2 (28 Sep 2026, research package 2) - research-only REFERENCE validator for grouped / pair-matrix schedule generation.
NOT Studio code, not the developer's generator and not the game's scheduling algorithm. Revision 1 (`overnight-research-2026-09-26/probes/
r123_schedule_generation_contract.py`, unchanged) stays the recorded coordinator-replayed result; this file imports its matrix / vector
helpers and replaces the request / proposal checks.

Changes from revision 1 (coordinator review 2026-09-28 finding 3):
  * Q11 validates the odd-host rule by VALUE: allowed 'lower_slot' | 'higher_slot' | 'balance' | {"a,b": host}. Codes:
      Q11  odd counts and no rule;           Q11r unsupported rule text / type ('balance' also refused on phased requests);
      Q11m malformed or non-canonical key;   Q11h host not one of the pair's two slots, or not an integer;
      Q11k an odd pair has no key;           Q11x a key names an even pair or a non-participant.
    JSON duplicate keys collapse in any dict parser - a production reader must reject them at parse time; this reference cannot see them.
  * 'balance' = a transcription of the developer's documented algorithm (schedule_edit.rs `OddHome::Balance`, read 28 Sep): home totals start
    at floor(count / 2) per pair; pairs i < j in participant order; host = the club with fewer home games so far, ties to the lower
    (count, slot) tuple; the host's total grows by one. The reference checks a proposal against that algorithm; it is not a game rule.
  * Rows carry their ORIGINAL POSITION (list position) and a STORED KEY (`index`) separately. The request table gives `stored_keys`
    (the source's key at every position; default = positions, for the revision-1 vectors). Kept rows carry `pos`.
      R2  kept rows: every stored value unchanged at the same position;
      R3  (revised) every row keeps the source's stored key of its position - a key is never rewritten to force key == position;
      Q13 the request's kept rows / stored keys are inconsistent with each other (position range, duplicate positions, key mismatch).
  * R5 now FAILS when an odd pair's host cannot be resolved (revision 1 silently skipped the host check for an unrecognised rule).
  * R11 (new) a generated game shares a date with a KEPT game of one of its clubs (stock mode: warning). Kept-only double bookings are
    reported as 'R9-retained' warnings, never failures. R9 keeps its revision-1 meaning (generated vs generated).
  * No date-packing rule around kept rows is checked (the developer's conservative packer is an implementation choice).
Stock replay (revision 2): reads each shipped table's stored `index` column (revision 1 used the position as the key), reports whether
stored keys equal positions, the generated-vs-kept and kept-only collisions, the relaxed checks and the fact that quotas / odd hosts are
derived from the same rows; Austrian phased tables get a static fact record (rows, tags, dates, pairs vs the R113 groups).
Usage: python r123r2_schedule_reference.py <r113.json> <out.json>
